proposed.explanation: Based on the verified FY2024 and FY2025 figures, COMI offers the most attractive combination of valuation and earnings scale for a medium-risk investor with a 7+ year horizon, so the recommendation is to buy 500 shares of COMI at 128.00 EGP per share for 64,000.00 EGP while retaining 16,000.00 EGP in cash. Telecom Egypt (ETEL) recorded the fastest net profit growth among the companies with verified two-year net profit data, rising 123.29% from 10,111,328,000 EGP in 2024 to 22,578,063,000 EGP in 2025. ETEL's basic and diluted EPS rose from 4.79 EGP in 2024 to 11.93 EGP in 2025, giving it the highest trailing P/E ratio in the group at 11.90x at the 141.95 EGP share price. Edita (EFID) achieved 67.75% net profit growth, increasing from 1,606,727,698 EGP in 2024 to 2,695,301,670 EGP in 2025. EFID's basic and diluted EPS doubled from 1.09 EGP in 2024 to 2.18 EGP in 2025, resulting in a trailing P/E ratio of 9.36x at 20.40 EGP per share. CIB (COMI) grew net profit by 48.87% from 55,256,732,000 EGP in 2024 to 82,258,815,000 EGP in 2025. COMI's basic EPS increased by 23.98% from 14.72 EGP in 2024 to 18.25 EGP in 2025, yielding the lowest P/E ratio of all four companies at 7.01x at 128.00 EGP per share. Talaat Moustafa (TMGH) reported 2025 consolidated net profit of 18,201,981,482 EGP, but a verified standalone 2024 net profit record is not present in the provided evidence (only 2025 gross profit was extracted instead and was not used for the net profit comparison), preventing a verified 2024-to-2025 net profit growth calculation for TMGH. However, TMGH's restated EPS rose 59.36% from 4.38 EGP in 2024 to 6.98 EGP in 2025, implying a trailing P/E ratio of 11.82x at 82.50 EGP per share. COMI is selected because it trades at the lowest earnings multiple (7.01x) alongside strong 48.87% net profit growth, offering a better valuation margin of safety for a medium-risk investor than ETEL (11.90x) or TMGH (11.82x), while retaining 16,000.00 EGP (20% of the portfolio) in cash limits single-stock concentration risk until 2026 interim results and balance-sheet metrics are reviewed; this guidance is not a guarantee of returns, and equity prices remain subject to market, macroeconomic, and banking-sector risks.
